articles.title_orig: Dow slides weighed by Home Depot; Nasdaq is flat ahead of Nvidia earnings: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Dow slides weighed by Home Depot; Nasdaq is flat ahead of Nvidia earnings: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Stocks were mixed Tuesday, as the Dow Jones Industrial Average struggled following the release of new corporate earnings reports, while chipmakers kept the Nasdaq Composite along the flatline. Investors also awaited Nvidia's quarterly release.
The Dow fell 306 points, or 0.6%. The Nasdaq was down 0.2%, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.3%.
Semiconductor names rose following a CNBC report that Anthropic would price its IPO above the current range of $70 to $78. Marvell Technology and Arm Holdings traded 2% and 1% higher, respectively. Broadcom also climbed 1%.
Home Depot dropped nearly 2% after the retailer announced a new CEO would take over next week, weighing on the Dow. That overshadowed better-than-expected quarterly results.
Those moves come as investors brace for Nvidia's quarterly report, due Tuesday after the bell.
Nvidia has been tumbling since last week. Jensen Huang resigned from the CEO post Thursday after reports emerged that he had multiple affairs , including one with an alleged Chinese spy . Further, the chipmaker's board of directors is not considering bringing Huang back as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. The stock has dropped almost 24% this month, putting it on pace for its biggest monthly decline since April 2022 — when it plunged 32%.
"The tape feels increasingly fragile as Nvidia's AI premium continues to unwind and investors reassess the durability of the ecosystem built around its dominance," said Ben Emons, founder of FedWatch Advisors, in a note. "This backdrop has fueled the 'dispersion trade,' gradually eroding the extreme concentration that has defined the S&P 500 and Nasdaq."
Investors are also poring over a slew of economic data on Tuesday, including October retail sales and import prices.
U.S. retail and food services sales rose 0.2% for the month to $748.2 billion, up 0.2% from September and in line with expectations.
Excluding the volatile gas and auto categories, retail sales rose 0.6% from the previous month. That's higher than the 0.4% expected on the Street.
On the earnings front, Disney and Home Depot are set to report before the opening bell.
The 30-stock Dow on Monday slid more than 700 points, or 1.4%, while the S&P 500 lost 1.9%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.5%, its biggest one-day decline since Nov. 5.
The Home Depot 's stock is under pressure despite the home improvement chain beating on both earnings and revenue and posting its strongest same-store sales growth in four years.
Shares of the retailer slipped nearly 3% on Tuesday.
Likely weighing on shares is the company's conservative implied outlook for the holiday season quarter amid ongoing housing headwinds and a cautious consumer environment.
Home Depot said it expects full-year adjusted EPS rising 2% from last year's $14.69 – leading to a projected EPS figure of $14.98 for this year. But after posting a 10-cent beat in the third quarter, that full-year projection implies fourth quarter adjusted EPS of $2.77 – solidly below the current consensus estimate of $2.81.
The retailer's same-store sales forecast is also underwhelming. Despite a slight beat in the just-completed quarter (up 2.2% vs. the Street's estimate of up 1.8%), Home Depot's projection of 1.4% same-store sales growth for this year is a hair below Wall Street's expectation for 1.5% growth.
U.S. equities were trading lower shortly after the opening bell on Tuesday.
The S&P 500 was down 0.3%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.6%, or 303 points. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite edged down 0.2%
Anthropic is likely to price its initial public offering above its proposed range of $70 to $78 a share, multiple sources told CNBC's David Faber on Tuesday.
The artificial intelligence company plans to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Nov. 19 under the ticker "ANT." The final offer price has yet to be set, according to CNBC's report .
St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem indicated Tuesday that the central bank may need as many as four rate hikes in coming months, offering one of the most hawkish views yet by a Fed policymaker about the steps needed to quell inflation.
During a speech delivered in Argentina, Musalem made the case that current policy is not significantly restricting economic activity.
"The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve 2% inflation in a timely manner," he said.
Read the full story below.
Spending in the retail sector rose 0.2% in October, matching expectations, though the ex-autos figure came in higher than forecast, the Commerce Department reported Tuesday.
A 1.6% decline in motor vehicle and parts sales held back the headline number, while a 4.7% surge in miscellaneous retailers helped offset other soft areas. Sales at gasoline stations rose 1.5% despite a general easing in energy prices.
In other economic news Tuesday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that import prices increased 1.1%, higher than the 0.7% estimate.
Nvidia reports earnings after the bell, and big investors may have shied away from it ahead of the release.
Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring noted that Nvidia "was the most 'under-owned' large-cap tech stock exiting the quarter."
"NVDA remained the most under-owned large-cap tech stock we track as of 3Q26 end, with the gap between NVDA's S&P 500 weighting and institutional ownership widening Q/Q by 22bps, ending 3Q26 at -2.75%, an all-time high. However, given NVDA shares have fallen 32% in the last 45 days vs. AAPL up 6%, it's highly plausible Apple could be the most under-owned mega-cap tech stock at present," he said.
The European Union's executive body on Tuesday upgraded its growth forecasts for the bloc, attributing an "upward surprise" across the first three quarters to a rebound in exports and solid consumption.
The European Commission's autumn report forecast euro area economic expansion of 1.4% in 2026, up from 1.1% in its spring forecast, followed by 1.4% growth in 2027, in line with its previous forecast.
That was despite a forecast of higher inflation pressures in the 21-nation euro area, estimated to hit an average 3.2% in 2026 and 3.1% in 2027, versus prior estimates of 3% and 2.2%. Euro zone inflation was 4% in October.
Energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain "severely disrupted," while freight and insurance costs have risen sharply, and bottlenecks in refining capacity and tight gas markets have all contributed to price pressures, the report said.
However, it said that medium-term inflation expectations were "well anchored," with markets remaining confident in the European Central Bank's ability to maintain price stability following 25 basis point rate hikes in June and September.
Rate hikes by central banks globally, rising government bond yields, uncertain trade policy, volatile stock markets and "concerns about the profitability and financing of AI companies" are all influencing the global economy, which is nonetheless continuing to expand amid strong growth in AI-related investment, it said.
"In 2026, Europe's economy is holding up better than expected. But we cannot take this for granted... We must safeguard our public finances, boost our competitiveness and lay the foundations for stronger long-term growth," Valdis Dombrovskis, Commissioner for Economy and Productivity, Implementation and Simplification, said in a statement.
Nvidia shares were down slightly on Tuesday, ahead of earnings and following days of decline as the company was rocked by Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO.
The chip giant briefly ticked up but was trading 0.28% down as of 5:05 AM ET in premarket deals.
— Kai Nicol-Schwarz, Jenni Reid
U.S. Treasury yields were little changed on Tuesday morning as investors awaited economic data and comments from Federal Reserve officials later in the session.

articles.title_orig: Bessent vs Lutnick: Who is winning the China chip debate?
articles.title_zh: Bessent vs Lutnick: Who is winning the China chip debate?
articles.content_orig:
A rift between United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over sales of advanced computer chips to China has spilled into public view.
On Monday, the administration of President Donald Trump introduced new rules requiring licences to sell advanced chips to buyers in named third countries suspected of being conduits to China. The new restrictions were written by Bessent’s Department of the Treasury and the White House – not Lutnick’s Department of Commerce, which usually oversees chip exports.
Trump, who is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China’s Shenzhen, has so far not taken a side.
As the US reels from the resignation of chip maker Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang last week over revelations that he had an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, here’s what this all means.
The two cabinet members, who are both veteran investors, disagree over how strictly the US should limit China’s access to the advanced chips that power artificial intelligence (AI).
The US restricts exports of certain advanced AI chips to China. In December 2025, Trump announced that Nvidia could sell its H200 chip to approved Chinese customers, on condition that 25 percent of the revenue would go to the US government. In January, the administration relaxed licensing rules for the H200 and similar chips.
On Monday, new controls were issued to monitor access to US chips in Southeast Asia and Brazil – penned by Bessent with the backing of the National Security Council, not by Lutnick.
As commerce secretary, Lutnick oversees these export controls and is charged with determining which critical technologies US companies can sell abroad, with an eye towards national security.
He has been one of the administration’s most vocal supporters of allowing Nvidia, the world’s dominant maker of AI super chips, to sell to China, despite the fact that it is racing against the US to dominate development of the AI industry.
“You want to sell the Chinese enough that their developers get addicted to the American technology stack,” Lutnick said in July 2025.
But US rules still bar the most advanced chips from being sold to China, and reports of restricted Nvidia chips allegedly being smuggled into the country through unofficial routes have put Lutnick’s role under the microscope.
Lutnick’s department was accused of turning a blind eye to such smuggling and stalling a planned crackdown on actors thought to be involved.
Fellow cabinet members and lawmakers have questioned his department’s handling of the issue, and some lawmakers say it has undermined US national security.
Bessent has pressed for tougher enforcement of existing export rules.
“We have all the authorities that we need. They just need to be implemented,” he said on Friday.
The two men have been rivals for some time. In 2024, Elon Musk and other Trump allies lobbied for Lutnick to get the Treasury job, but it ultimately went to Bessent.
Nvidia controls nearly 90 percent of the market for the most advanced chips used for AI. Worth trillions of dollars, it is among the world’s most valuable companies, and its customers include tech giants Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta.
Nvidia’s cofounder and chief executive, Jensen Huang, resigned last week after admitting to an affair with Alice Huang, whom some US officials have suspected of working for Chinese intelligence – a claim denied by China.
Alice Huang is a former senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that builds data centres in Southeast Asia which cater for Chinese clients.
Megaspeed bought more than $4.8bn of Nvidia chips in about two years, but US authorities suspect that many of these chips were then smuggled into China rather than used in Megaspeed’s data centres, a charge it denies.
On Friday, Bessent said four government agencies, including the Treasury, had pushed for months to put Megaspeed on a US trade blacklist, but Lutnick’s Commerce Department had not acted.
“Commerce has the pen,” Bessent told CNBC. “You will have to ask them about their internal processes.”
He also questioned whether Nvidia had properly vetted its customers.
“The real story here should be, did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?” Bessent said.
The new rules require companies to obtain a US licence before shipping advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil – countries Washington suspects of acting as conduit routes for chips to reach China.
It also requires any data centre in the world using Nvidia chips to obtain Washington’s permission before it can “rent” computer power to Chinese customers. This closes a loophole that previously allowed Chinese companies to “rent” the use of advanced chips without purchasing them outright.
China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the restrictions as “economic coercion” and said Beijing would take “necessary measures” in response.
In Washington, the new restrictions were welcomed by John Moolenaar, the Republican chair of the House Select Committee on China.
The committee, a panel of lawmakers focused on competition with China’s ruling Communist Party, is one of the most hawkish voices on Beijing in Congress. Moolenaar criticised the administration’s decision last year to ease curbs on Nvidia’s chip sales to China.
“Our most advanced AI chips are simply not for sale to our foremost enemy,” he said.
Senior officials including Secretary of State Marco Rubio and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer have argued for keeping the most advanced chips out of China, while lawmakers from both parties have criticised Lutnick.
“It would be dumb and stupid for us to sell that to anybody, especially a country that’s going to reverse-engineer it and leapfrog us,” Rubio said in May.
Greer made a similar case last week, saying that US “crown jewels” should remain in US hands or in the hands of allies.
David Sacks, Trump’s former AI adviser, however, defended selling chips to China and dismissed those pushing for tighter controls.
“The policy of the China hawks is effectively the policy of the CCP [Chinese Communist Party]. Neither one wants American chips in China,” he said in a podcast appearance on Saturday.
On the other side of the political aisle, some Democrats have called for Lutnick to step down from his position for his failure to police chip smuggling.
“Making powerful Nvidia chips available to China through an apparent spy undercut both national security and economic competitiveness,” Senator Richard Blumenthal said in a post on X.
Both Lutnick and Jensen Huang have been summoned to testify before the Senate on December 3.
Trump has swung between restricting and allowing Nvidia’s sales to China. In April 2025, the White House curbed sales of the H20, a chip Nvidia made for the Chinese market – only to agree to allow them three months later.
His later decision in December to permit sales of the more powerful H200 marked a further easing of those restrictions.
Trump has stood by Lutnick, saying on Monday that he was not planning to remove him, days after the Reuters news agency reported that top White House aides had debated whether he should go.
Trump has acknowledged that the issue is splitting his cabinet, without explicitly taking sides.
“It’s a different viewpoint. One wants to be friendly with China and one wants to have a blowup with China,” Trump said. “They both are acceptable, but they are different views.”
Trump has also said it “certainly isn’t a bad idea” for Huang to return to Nvidia .
Trump and Xi are due to meet in Shenzhen on Thursday, during this week’s APEC summit. Ahead of their last meeting , when Xi visited the US in September, Washington banned imports of Chinese-made humanoid robots and threatened to sanction Chinese AI f

articles.title_orig: China says it will take countermeasures if US imposes new chip curbs
articles.title_zh: China says it will take countermeasures if US imposes new chip curbs
articles.content_orig:
Xi and Trump when they met in Beijing in May
As US President Donald Trump heads to China, his administration has renewed efforts to curb Beijing's access to advanced semiconductors.
On Monday, Washington announced new interim rules that will increase scrutiny of  data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.
The move not only restricts the export of advanced chips, but also access to their computing power, which Chinese firms currently rent abroad to train artificial intelligence (AI) models.
South East Asian countries in particular have invested heavily in data centres to power their AI ambitions - and Chinese firms seeking computing power overseas have been a key market.
But now these firms will need a US government licence to buy advanced chips from Nvidia or other American chipmakers. This allows Washington to monitor if those chips are being used to serve Chinese companies, or being smuggled to China.
This poses a fresh challenge for Beijing, which has become deeply dependent on compute from abroad in the wake of US export restrictions. At least 30% of China's advanced AI computing power is projected to come from renting overseas or smuggling in 2027, according to research by the Institute for Progress , external , a US-based think-tank.
China's foreign ministry called the new rules "economic coercion" and said Beijing "will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own legitimate rights and interests".
This is also a problem for South East Asian economies where large numbers of data centres have sprung up recently. Some of the firms behind them are accused of helping China evade US export controls on advanced chips.
One of those is Singaporean data centre firm Megaspeed, whose former director Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese spy. Calls for tighter export controls have grown after Nvidia's Jensen Huang admited to an affair with her and resigned as CEO .
Megaspeed, the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia, is accused of illegally smuggling chips to Chinese companies after purchasing them for use in data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
The company has denied these allegations, defended its business as "legitimate and lawful", and said it has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation". It also said Alice Huang stepped down from her role as director in late 2023 and left the firm last year.
The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, however, has said Brazil and the four South East Asian nations "present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion" of the chips that Washington wants to keep out of China's hands.
The new measures are aimed at ensuring sensitive US technology "cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries," the bureau added. Licences will be issued on a "case-by-case basis", it said.
Batam in Indonesia is emerging as a major regional data centre hub
Countries like Malaysia and Thailand whose data centre roll out has been heavily driven by Chinese buyers could be hit hardest, says international trade expert Naoise McDonagh from Australia's Edith Cowan University.
But the new rules are unlikely to derail the data centre boom as a whole, says Reema Bhattacharya from advisory firm Verisk Maplecroft, adding that investment backed by major tech firms and clearly identifiable customers should "remain relatively resilient".
Singapore was an early adopter of data centres but when it began limiting new construction, investment flowed to neighbours Malaysia and Thailand. Johor in Malaysia and Batam in Indonesia have also approved billions of dollars worth of data centres to catch the spillover demand.
These countries have been offering incentives such as cheaper land to attract foreign investment, including from Chinese tech giants Alibaba and Tencent.
But now, the region could find it harder to get hold of advanced chips.
The BBC has contacted Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand for comment.
Singapore said it is "engaging relevant US authorities" to understand the new rules better, and is "exploring how to facilitate trusted access" for local firms.
A spokesperson for Brazil's Ministry of Development, Industry, Trade and Services said it is aware of the US announcement and it "is closely monitoring any potential developments regarding this measure".
Malaysia previously said it welcomes data centre investment but "will not allow itself to be used to get around export controls".
The new rules also come just ahead of Trump's meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen this week.
Beijing has made self-sufficiency in tech a national priority and needs the best chips to build powerful AI models.
Chinese firms DeepSeek and MoonShot have come close to US rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI. So much so that The Institute for Progress estimates top US AI models lead the best Chinese platforms by only about six and half months.
"This is despite US AI companies having significantly better compute access and financing," it said.
Still, China needs advanced US chips to ensure its best AI models are competitive, experts tell the BBC.
The new restrictions on South East Asia and Brazil have taken away "one of the more practical routes Chinese AI developers had to accessing frontier computing power," Bhattacharya said.
But tighter restrictions could also push Chinese firms towards domestic semiconductors and further drive advancement at home.
That has been a longstanding dilemma for Washington, McDonagh said: whether to keep selling chips to China to retain its reliance on the US, or restrict access and risk further spurring Chinese innovation.

articles.title_orig: Putin Is Open to Meeting With North Korea’s Leader in China, Kremlin Says
articles.title_zh: Putin Is Open to Meeting With North Korea’s Leader in China, Kremlin Says
articles.content_orig:
President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia could meet with Kim Jong-un if the North Korean leader travels to China for the APEC summit this week, the Kremlin said, reflecting the deepening of ties between their countries in recent years.
Asked about the possibility of a meeting, Dmitri S. Peskov, the Kremlin spokesman, said on Monday that it would “of course” happen if Mr. Kim went to Shenzhen, the Chinese economic hub and host city, according to Russian state news agencies. North Korea has not confirmed whether Mr. Kim plans to attend the summit.
Mr. Putin and Mr. Kim have publicly met three times since 2022, and North Korea has been a key supporter of Russia’s military actions in Ukraine.
As the war in Ukraine nears its fifth anniversary, with no end in sight, the Kremlin is expected to use Mr. Putin’s many meetings at the APEC summit to showcase how Russia is regarded as one of the major international powers alongside the United States and China.
A visit by Mr. Kim would be a rare foray outside North Korea for the leader, and it would further raise the prospect that he could meet with President Trump in China. On the first day of his 48-hour trip to Asia, Mr. Trump told reporters that Mr. Kim “would like” to come to the APEC summit. The president has repeatedly said he would like to meet with Mr. Kim again.
On Wednesday, Mr. Putin is scheduled to meet with Xi Jinping, China’s leader. On Thursday, he is set to take part in a trilateral summit with Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump, the first meeting of its kind. The Kremlin said on Monday that it was working to arrange a bilateral meeting between Mr. Putin and Mr. Trump.
Before his departure for China, Mr. Putin met on Monday in the Kremlin with Jo Yong-won, a secretary of North Korea’s ruling Workers’ Party. During the meeting, Mr. Putin said that North Korea’s help in driving Ukrainian forces from the Kursk region of Russia last year “marked a new chapter in the history of military cooperation between our countries.”
Moscow planned to unveil a monument in Kursk by the end of the year to honor the North Korean troops, Mr. Putin said.
Ivan Nechepurenko covers Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, the countries of the Caucasus and Central Asia. He divides his reporting time between Moscow and Tbilisi, Georgia.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia forms export-control panel as Huang affair puts China ties in focus
articles.title_zh: Nvidia forms export-control panel as Huang affair puts China ties in focus
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia on Tuesday said its board has formed a committee to oversee its national security policies and compliance with U.S. export controls, a step that comes amid heightened scrutiny of the chipmaker's sales practices to some Southeast Asian companies.
The move comes days after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO over revelations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, as well as a subordinate at the company. The woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation), had worked for a Singapore-based data center company, Megaspeed, which had bought billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia chips.
The arrangements between Nvidia and Megaspeed have heightened concerns that China and other nations could access Nvidia's advanced chips by renting computing resources via data centers in Singapore and other Southeast Asian countries. The U.S. has barred sales of Nvidia's highest-end chips, used in artificial intelligence, to China due to national security and competitive concerns.
On Monday, the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim rule limiting other countries' access to advanced chips that power artificial intelligence.
Nvidia said the company's existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report directly to the new committee and to its interim CEO, Colette Kress.
"Nvidia recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security," Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board of directors, said in a statement.
The company added that the decision to create the committee reflects the board's commitment "to demonstrate the highest standards of governance and oversight."

articles.title_orig: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
articles.title_zh: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
articles.content_orig:
Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all.
The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user’s knowledge.
Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent’s reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. When one of the employees asked the bot if it made any accesses, it checked twice and then outputted: “Overnight into Friday morning I was idle.”
The NewCore employees sent the gateway logs to Grok Bot support personnel and asked what was causing the bots to access accounts without prompting or approval. The support team’s reply indicated the behavior was by design and intended to allow the bots to proactively take actions on behalf of users. In other words, the unrequested and unlogged access attempts were a feature designed to make Grok Bot more useful by periodically checking in and finding tasks to perform before a user even asks. The proactive check-in is a feature of Cursor, the AI coding service SpaceXSI recently acquired.
“There is no bug to patch, which is exactly why this is worse than a bug,” Ido Hoorvitch, a NewCore security researcher, wrote in an email. “A vulnerability gets fixed. This is the product working as designed: an agent that holds your credentials, acts under your identity while you sleep, ignores the one refusal you can give it, and then tells you it did nothing.”
Hoorvitch said that Grok Bot provides minimal notification of the automatic “turns,” or the cycles that occur when an agent receives instructions or context, decides what to do, and calls whatever tools it chooses. The notice comes during onboarding when the bot says it keeps working while the user is away from the computer and connects to apps and uses them the way the user does.
“It reads like a welcome message and scrolls off the screen in under a minute,” Hoorvitch said. “Nobody is asked to consent to it. Nothing says the platform will start turns with no message from you, or that those turns will use your connectors.”
The researcher said that Grok Bot documentation notes that a primary bot checks in on its own, and a changelog mentions brief background wakes, but there is no mention that the check-ins “reach into your connected apps.” Further, once a check-in runs, there is no mention of it in the chat interface or in the chat history, and as already noted, prompts to stop check-ins don’t work. Hoorvitch said the bot “always asks before making changes,” but that applies only to events in which data or changes are written to an app.
NewCore contacted Grok Bot support on November 4. At the time, users had no way to turn off the automatic check-ins. Then, eight days later, Hoorvitch said, the Cursor dashboard, the administrative console behind Grok Bot, received an update. Under bot capabilities, a new toggle called proactive messages appeared. By default, it’s set to on. When a team admin sets it to off, bots no longer run check-ins on their own.
SpaceXSI representatives didn’t answer questions sent by email.

articles.title_orig: American shoppers are showing signs of strain heading into the holiday season
articles.title_zh: American shoppers are showing signs of strain heading into the holiday season
articles.content_orig:
Americans pulled back on some purchases last month, as  high gas prices and ongoing cost-of-living concerns continued to weigh on some household budgets, new data showed Tuesday.
US retail sales rose 0.2% in October, a slowdown after gas prices drove a 0.8% gain the month before, according to Commerce Department data released Tuesday.
October’s spending tally was driven lower by a drop in car sales, which offset a more modest uptick in gasoline station sales (which slowed to a gain of 1.5% versus a 6% increase the month before), data showed.
Retail sales are adjusted for seasonal swings but not inflation, which rose 0.4% in October, Consumer Price Index data shows.
In addition to falling sales of cars, Tuesday report showed consumers reined in purchases on furniture, sporting goods and apparel; and cut back a little on their food spending.
October’s tepid spending, however, could be a sign that some consumers may be gearing up for the holiday shopping season, said Elizabeth Renter, lead economist at Life360.
“Several of the categories where spending declined are discretionary categories – purchases you can put off for a while because you don’t need those goods every single month,” she wrote in a note Tuesday. “Because this is October data, savvy families may be saving those purchases for holiday sale deals.”
To be sure, a closely watched category of spending that strips out some more volatile areas (such as gasoline stations, auto sales, building materials and restaurants) rose at a stronger-than-expected rate of 0.6%, a tick higher than a 0.5% gain notched in September.
Sales at miscellaneous stores (a catch-all category that includes retailers in pet supplies, office goods, florists etc.) saw the biggest gains in October, at 4.7%, while spending remained firm at health and personal care stores as well as online retailers (Amazon, for example, held a sales event early last month).
“We wouldn’t say consumers are splurging, but they certainly aren’t retrenching,” Oren Klachkin, Nationwide financial markets economist, wrote in a note to investors Tuesday. “High prices and interest rates are making some trade down and be more judicious, but solid fundamentals and a boost from early holiday shopping are keeping consumers in a spending mood.”
Tuesday’s report underscored the ongoing bifurcation of household finances, ING chief international economist James Knightley said, noting the differing trajectories of spending among high-income individuals versus middle- and lower-income Americans.
“Middle- and lower-income households tend to spend more of their income of physical goods, such as food and clothing, and squeezed spending power limits the potential for growth,” he wrote. “Conversely, high income households have seen their wealth surge, boosting consumption, and are accounting for a growing share of total consumer spending.”
In addition to Tuesday’s retail sales data, a fuller picture of consumer health and spending could come via Target and Walmart, which are slated to release their latest earnings reports on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively, this week.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia shares set for $335 billion swing after earnings, options show
articles.title_zh: Nvidia shares set for $335 billion swing after earnings, options show
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting big moves.
With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the company that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.
"Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, said in a text ahead of the company's after-market report on Tuesday.
Since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is currently 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.
The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.
One catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.
With bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.
By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.
Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

articles.title_orig: Deutsche Bank Leak Reveals $582 Million In Epstein Payments, Accidental Trump Tax Disclosure
articles.title_zh: Deutsche Bank Leak Reveals $582 Million In Epstein Payments, Accidental Trump Tax Disclosure
articles.content_orig:
Deutsche Bank’s headquarters in Frankfurt. The bank long resisted breaking with Russia’s most important business titans under President Vladimir V. Putin. Credit... Felix Schmitt for The New York Times
By Russ Buettner Khadija Sharife Brian Fitzpatrick Frederik Obermaier Bastian Obermayer and Sophia Baumann
When Russian missiles began pummeling Ukraine in February 2022, executives at one of the world’s largest banks sensed trouble headed their way.
Within hours of an invasion that set off a war that is now in its fifth year, Western governments issued new financial sanctions intended to further isolate Russia from the world economy.
At Deutsche Bank, a longtime bank of Russian industry titans and oligarchs, officials scrambled to get ahead of the damage. “Russian Sanctions Urgent Request” read the subject line of an email sent by one of Deutsche’s anti-financial crime specialists to her colleagues.
“As you know we have a large Russian Oligarchs client population” and other clients with investments in Russian companies, she wrote. She asked which of those clients “we potentially could unwind and which not.” Should the bank advise them, she wondered, to withdraw their money “while they still can?”
This email exchange was the beginning of a frenzied reckoning within the scandal-plagued bank over its long resistance to breaking with Russia’s most important business titans under Vladimir V. Putin, the Russian president. The bank’s clients included the Russian billionaires Oleg V. Deripaska and Viktor F. Vekselberg. Time and again over many years, records show, Deutsche Bank’s risk managers warned that such relationships were perilous.
But profits associated with maintaining its Russian clients won out every time.
Russia’s war in Ukraine swept up Deutsche Bank in a larger shift. For decades, German politicians and business leaders believed that working with Russia and deepening economic ties between the two countries would discourage Russian aggression. That strategy collapsed after the invasion.

articles.title_orig: Putin's Crimea bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Putin's Crimea bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.
Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge has collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort.
The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before" and that Russian President Vladimir Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack.
The bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014, and was personally opened by Putin in 2018.
Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.
While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Putin.
The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight.
The damage after the overnight attack, involving missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section of the bridge apparently destroyed.
Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below.
Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective".
He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage".
The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and a Russian-backed official said some rail services were operating.
Ukraine's state security service SBU said operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders".
Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China.
Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations".
For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry.
Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday.
Elsewhere, Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - were closed after Russia hit Ukraine's capital overnight.
Loud explosions were heard in Kyiv just before midnight on Tuesday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies.
Some of Kyiv's above-ground metro services were damaged in the overnight attacks, local officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters.
Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city.
Strikes on the busy Northern and Southern Bridges will cause major disruption to people's daily lives.
Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials.
The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly.
The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired.
However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar.
This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.
There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack.
Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.
In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel.
This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdiansk.
Russia's launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control.

articles.title_orig: Mongolia’s president says he will step down after facing accusations of corruption
articles.title_zh: Mongolia’s president says he will step down after facing accusations of corruption
articles.content_orig:
Mongolian President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa said Tuesday that he would resign after the opposition Democratic Party accused him of profiting from a government railway project.
At a press conference, Khurelsukh said he was being "falsely accused and defamed" but would resign in order to "restore my good name."
He has pledged to cooperate with investigators.
Before the resignation takes effect, it must first be accepted by parliament, the State Great Khural.
Nyambaatar Khishgee, the ex-mayor of Ulaanbaatar, the country's capital, on Saturday accused Khurelsukh of receiving $25 million (around €23 million) linked to the Tavantolgoi-Gashuunsukhait railway project.
The railway connects the Tavantolgoi coal mine with the Mongolian port of Gashuunsukhait on the Chinese border, a central hub for the export of coal from Mongolia to China.
The former mayor belongs to the president's party, but is part of a different faction within it.
The opposition Democratic Party picked up on the accusations and called on Khurelsukh to step down.
According to the allegations, Khurelsukh received the money in bribes from the conglomerate Bodi International LLC, which received the contract to construct the railway without a competitive tender.
Bodi on Monday denied having paid any cash bribes to obtain the contract.
Khurelsukh, from the Mongolian People's Party, has been president since 2021.
But infighting has caused disruption in the party in recent years, with three prime ministers taking office in just nine months.
Khurelsukh paid a state visit to Germany from October 19 to 22 this year.

articles.title_orig: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
articles.title_zh: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
articles.content_orig:
The UK has sanctioned companies it said were involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
The government said the sanctions against eight construction and property development firms would disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support building in the West Bank.
Settlements are illegal under international law, and there has been a rise in violence towards Palestinians in the West Bank by settlers in recent months.
It comes two days before the deadline for bids for construction tenders in the E1 area east of Jerusalem.
The plans, which have been condemned internationally, would in effect divide the West Bank in two and isolate East Jerusalem.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said the E1 development would render a two-state solution "unviable" by "cutting through the heart of Palestine".
The sanctions also target Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement which the UK government says has organised and carried out blockades to prevent aid entering Gaza.
It comes after the UK expanded its human rights sanctions regime last month, enabling the government to sanction individuals and companies involved in violations of international humanitarian law anywhere in the world.
The government is also developing separate legislation to ban the import of settlement goods and the provision of advertising services for settlement properties in the UK.
Miliband said: "Protecting the two-state solution is the North Star of this government's approach.
"That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution.
"The status quo in the West Bank and Gaza is unacceptable.
"We are committed to working productively with a new Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority to advance lasting peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians alike."
In September, the UK government announced that it would ban the import of goods from Israeli settlements, as well as acting against companies and individuals providing services for settlement expansion.
At the time, Miliband said the move marked the "beginning of a new approach" to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, which "not only calls out injustice and suffering but acts".
The announcement prompted a furious reaction from Israel .
Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them.
There has been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.

articles.title_orig: Neurable One Review: The Brain-Scanning Headphones That Helped Me Stay Focused
articles.title_zh: Neurable One Review: The Brain-Scanning Headphones That Helped Me Stay Focused
articles.content_orig:
The cans hide a wearable EEG that tracks your attention.
I've always been fascinated by the inner workings of the human mind , and I've tested plenty of brain gadgets in my time. Sadly, all of them have been so clunky that they can only really be worn in the privacy of your own home. At least, that was the case. The Neurable One actually buries its brain-scanning technology into a pair of beefy over-ear headphones. It's designed to keep an eye on your focus levels and attention while you work, or meditate, wherever you are.
The company describes it as a "fitness tracker for your brain," so when your attention starts to drift, the headphones will remind you to keep your focus where it needs to be. And, if things continue to go wayward, you'll be advised to take a break and come back fresh rather than burning out halfway through the day. In that regard, it's been fascinating to see how the system thinks my brain operates on a regular basis.
The Neurable One is cheaper than its predecessors and its competitors, and Neurable has improved its software platform. If there's a downside, it's that as much as I've loved my time with them, it's hard to think anyone other than nerds like me will want to use them.
Neurable spun out of a project from the University of Michigan in 2015, with the goal of building Brain Computer Interfaces (BCIs) and algorithms to interpret that data. The focus is on cognitive performance as there's plenty of military and civilian applications for the technology. Despite the name, Neurable One is actually the third pair of EEG headphones the company has made. In 2024, it partnered with Master & Dynamic on the MW75 Neuro, and a year later the Neuro LT, a lighter version of the same product addressing user comfort issues. This time out, Neurable is going it alone without the backing of any fancy audio brands.
At a glance, you'll struggle to notice much difference between this and its predecessors, as any variances are mostly aesthetic tweaks. Button placements are the same, but they're now pill-shaped rather than the circles found on the older models. The logo on the earcups has changed from M&D's icon to Neurable's signature brainwave, and there are fewer vents. In fact, the biggest difference is the loss of the cantilevered armatures joining the headband to the earcups, which have been replaced with standard hardware here.
It's a similar story inside the body as well; the Neurable One is more or less equipped with the same gear as before. You'll get the same 40mm Beryllium drivers, Bluetooth 5.2, AAC and aptX, albeit with six microphones — down from the eight on the MW75 Neuro. As before, each earcup has a series of dry-fit EEG sensors woven into the earpads which sit around your ear.
Neurable's pitch is to help people gain deeper insights into their own cognitive performance through the day. It contends that, much like the rest of our body, our minds have enough fuel to get us through the day, but not at full-tilt, full-pelt output. The company says it's a better idea to, when your attention and focus starts to wane, take a break ahead of you burning out. Neurable argues that spending a quick five minutes staring out of the window is better than getting a headache and not functioning for an hour.
Strap the headphones on at the start of the day and the system will keep an eye on how you're doing. Do this over a period of days, or weeks, and you'll get a sense of where your focus is at its highest and lowest. You can then adjust your working patterns to suit those stats. The Neurable One works equally well when you're meditating or relaxing, giving you insights as to how and when your mind rests.
One of my eternal gripes with a lot of wearable EEGs (and other fabric sensors more broadly) is that the sensor pads are often fussy. They often don't work at all if they're bone dry and the skin they're in contact with is dry as well, which frustrates me. I've regularly had to gently dab the pads with cold water before running a washcloth across my forehead to dampen it. But, if the skin and pads are too wet, you'll be given a warning to dry both out, which slows you down even further. Thankfully, the Neurable One's dry-fit sensors worked from the get-go more or less every time I've used them. Every now and again, I'll be asked to push my (short) hair away from around my ears to improve the connection, but it's a world away from other products in the same field that I've tested.
Setup is a breeze, and the process of beginning your first session is relatively effortless, as is the daily routine you're expected to fall into. That begins with a check in at the start of the day, closing your eyes and triggering a 60-second scan of your brain. You'll get a dashboard containing your scores, with a comparison to the day before to see if things got better or worse. If you had a rough night, or if there's a lot going on, you can journal some notes on the same pane.
What's far more interesting and useful are the Insights and Improve sections, which tell you both what to do to manage your cognitive load right now, and how to boost it. The former suggests that you delay big decisions, not starting jobs that need a lot of attention and grouping small, repetitive tasks together. The latter asks you to go for a quick walk in the sun, go sit in another room away from your computer for five minutes or to write down all of the things sitting in your mental cache. Once done, you can run another check-in to see if that's made any improvement.
If I'm honest, I was having a busy day at the start of a busy week, and felt snowed under by all of the projects on my desk. (In fact, my biggest issue, throughout testing these headphones, was that my Cognitive Load was always problematically high. It's almost as if working in journalism and juggling hundreds of projects all at once is somehow a problem.) The app told me that I was running low, but said I should walk up and down my stairs for a few minutes and then come back and check again. And, wouldn't you know, it actually did improve both my score and my ability to get stuff done for the rest of the morning.
Most days, I would set the EEG running at 9AM or so and not take them off until 12 or 1PM. The app will keep track of how well it thinks you're concentrating, letting you see that as a real time figure on screen. If it detects your focus beginning to drift, it'll rouse you back, but after a while, if you still struggle to concentrate, it'll advise you to take a short break. One thing I don't like is the way the system prods you to get back on track: When it thinks your focus is waning, you'll get a ping played in your ear as a sort of "come on, pay attention" trigger.
It's a harsh noise, and one that would distract me as often as it did help me drift back toward focus. You can shut off this guidance in the app, but I persevered with them even when it put me in mind of a '70s kung fu B-movie where the protagonist is asked to build a house of cards while being pelted with rotten fruit. Regularly, I'd be halfway through writing a line in what I'd describe as a flow state and then I'd get pinged, knocking me off my train of thought.
But the more I used the headphones, the more I was able to see when the system said I was doing well and what caused slips. It became an increasingly positive feedback loop where I'd scrub through the timeline of my morning to see what I was doing when my focus was high.
As for audio quality, it's clear the company has tried to sail close to Master & Dynamic's promise of warm bass and clear treble. There's a wonderful atmosphere to the sound that makes you feel like you're in the room when it was recorded. One of my favourite tracks to test headphones with is "Finale" from the Tron: Legacy soundtrack where you can hear the horn player's breath. Wearing these, I was equally delighted to feel the rumble of the kettle drums pushing the air to my ear as they crescendoed.

articles.title_orig: GTA 6: How one school is battling the 'GTA flu' with warnings to parents and prizes for pupils
articles.title_zh: GTA 6: How one school is battling the 'GTA flu' with warnings to parents and prizes for pupils
articles.content_orig:
A school concerned about pupils not coming in on the day the highly-anticipated GTA VI video game is released has offered young people prizes for turning up for classes.
Belfast Boys' Model school issued letters to parents, saying that the release of the game on Thursday coincided with GCSE maths exams.
The school said that "activities such as playing Grand Theft Auto can wait until the weekend".
On Monday, the school added that pupils who attended school on both Thursday and Friday would be entered into a draw for a £70 gift card for either PlayStation or Xbox.
In a letter issued to parents, reported by The Nolan Show , the school reminded "all parents and carers of the importance of ensuring that students attend school on Thursday 19th November".
It also said that "all Year 11 students and some Year 12 students" would be sitting a GCSE maths exam on Thursday, the same day the game comes out.
"Good attendance is one of the strongest indicators of academic success," the letter added.
Mary Montgomery, who is principal of the school, said "the primary focus" of her letter was Thursday's Mathematics examination and "encouraging our boys to be in school and ready to achieve their best".
"The results at GCSE have been fantastic in recent years and we want to continue that success for the boys," she said.
"It also highlighted the launch of GTA as something which might entice some boys to stay at home. However, the games vouchers were a pupil-led incentive."
GTA VI is released on Thursday, 13 years after the previous edition and with an estimated development cost of more $1bn (£866m).
In 2013, the term 'GTA Flu' was coined in reference to the large number of sick days reportedly taken when GTA V was released.
On Monday, the school announced that all pupils in attendance on Thursday and Friday would be entered into a draw to win one of two £70 gift cards "for PlayStation/Xbox".
The school's head boy said "the idea came from us as pupils".
"We wanted to do something positive to mark International Men's Day and, importantly, to raise money for a charity that supports male victims of domestic violence," he said.
"For us, the most important thing was having as many boys as possible in school so everyone could get involved and support the fundraising."
He added that gaming can help the pupils "switch off and manage some of the stress around exams, which is important with GCSE modules this week".
Speaking to The Nolan Show, a former school principal Kathleen O'Hare said the decision to send the letter to parents was "very wise".
"The cult of this game is so large that parents will be put under extreme pressure at times," she said.
O'Hare added that it has been "proven" that missing a day of school "really does matter".
Pete Wray, a Ulster Unionist Party councillor who works with children, said "there is a sizable amount of young people that are in our education system and completely disengage".
"They take an odd day off, and once they've got one day off, they're anxious about going back because they know they're going to be behind, and that leads to more and more problems," he said.
Wray said he will be imploring young people not to miss school to play the game, but that he "completely understands how people can become engrossed in it".
Considered one of the most highly-anticipated video games in history, the game is the latest in the long-running Grand Theft Auto series.
The game series, which has attracted controversy in the past over its depiction of violence and crime, is also the most expensive game ever made, with estimates putting development costs at more than $1bn (£866m).
The previous game in the series, GTA 5, sold nearly 230 million copies, making it one of the best-selling games of all time, which has generated billions of dollars in revenue for developer Rockstar.
GTA 6 will feature its first ever playable female protagonist in a 3D setting - Lucia - alongside her partner in life and crime, Jason, as a second playable character.
Like other GTA games before it, the sixth chapter is set in a fictional US state - this time in Leonida, which is Rockstar's version of Florida.

articles.title_orig: Nike hosts first investor day in 9 years as it tries to rightsize its business
articles.title_zh: Nike hosts first investor day in 9 years as it tries to rightsize its business
articles.content_orig:
Nike said Tuesday ahead of its first investor day in nine years that it was reaffirming its 2027 financial guidance.
The retailer also laid out a financial framework and said that by the end of fiscal 2031 it's targeting approximately $5 billion in incremental revenue growth from fiscal year 2027, operating margins of 12% to 14% and adjusted earnings per share of $3.00 to $3.50. The company said higher-quality revenue, gross margin expansion and productivity improvements would help it reach its goals.
Nike's 2027 financial guidance includes expectations for revenue to decline in the high-single-digit range, an adjusted operating margin of approximately 6%, and adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35.
The company also introduced a strategy it's calling Full Stride Ahead, which the company said aims "to get closer to athletes and focus resources on the greatest opportunities for long-term growth."
"We're concentrating our resources where we have the greatest potential to win," Nike CEO Elliott Hill said in a statement. "We're also changing how we operate — delivering breakthrough products, building deeper local connections and moving faster to capture demand. Together, these actions are designed to return NIKE to sustainable, profitable growth."
Nike said it would focus on performance sports and sportswear opportunities "with the greatest potential for long-term growth," and said its five priority sports would be running, training, global football, basketball and outdoor.
Nike is holding an investor day at its Oregon headquarters Tuesday as the company aims to prove to investors that its turnaround strategy is yielding success after a yearslong slump.
Last month, the company reported mixed fiscal first-quarter results as it announced a restructuring plan, including layoffs that it said would start next year. It's the company's third round of layoffs to be announced this year.
Nike's net income and revenue both fell during the most recent period compared with a year ago, and the company said it expects revenue to decline by a high single-digit percentage in fiscal 2027.
The new strategy, dubbed Pace, focuses on the company's supply chain and reorganizing into three geographies. Nike said the turnaround plan is expected to deliver roughly $2.5 billion in savings through fiscal 2031.
Nike has been seeing significant sustained declines in its China market, where revenue last quarter dropped 26%. Experts have said the company is losing relevance in the country, while Nike has said it's actively working to win over younger consumers.
At the same time, Nike announced last quarter that it's creating a new global campus in India as part of its new growth strategy, hoping the country will help boost its performance. The company said it was remaining focused on China even as it begins to build out its India presence.
CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround strategy includes improving different parts of the business at different rates based on priority. While it's seen some signs of progress in the North America business, Hill has said that performance isn't enough to offset the pressures on the company elsewhere, including internationally.
The Nike consumer has also been under increased macroeconomic pressure as geopolitical tensions mount and inflation rises.
Shares of Nike have fallen 50% over the past two years.

articles.title_orig: Push to reinstate Jensen Huang tests superstar tech CEO accountability
articles.title_zh: Push to reinstate Jensen Huang tests superstar tech CEO accountability
articles.content_orig:
CEO ousted after affair with suspected Chinese spy reportedly plans comeback, but US treasury secretary urges ‘dramatic shake-up’
Megaspeed says it’s a ‘legitimate and lawful business’
Business live – latest updates
Elon Musk and a host of other tech bosses have called for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia, amid reports the former chief executive is already plotting a return to the chip company just four days after his resignation.
An open letter that has more than 165,000 signatories demands that the company’s board members “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”.
Huang’s resignation on Thursday ended a 33-year run at the helm of the AI company he co-founded, after reports he had at least two extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China and another with a subordinate.
According to the Financial Times , Huang has discussed a possible return to the company with people close to him. One Huang ally told the paper they were putting together ⁠a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby ​for the former Nvidia ‌CEO’s return ‌and would try to garner support from ‌the White House.
“Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” the person said, adding that the efforts had Huang’s support.
On Friday, two big shareholders, the investors Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker, urged the board to keep “all options” open.
In Washington, however, the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, argued on Sunday that Nvidia should look outside the company for its next CEO. “They need a dramatic shake-up,” Bessent said on Fox News.
Bessent also called on Nvidia to explain whether it had knowingly allowed its most advanced AI chips to reach China, saying this was more important than Huang’s affair with the alleged spy for Beijing, Alice Huang.
The US forbids sales to China of the most cutting-edge AI chips as parts of its strategy to stay ahead of Beijing in the race to dominate artificial intelligence.
In late 2025, Trump authorised sales of Nvidia chips called H200s to China, but not the most advanced chips used to run AI models reshaping modern society.
“Nothing above the H200s can be sold to the Chinese,” Bessent said, adding that it was important to examine “whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance around the US export restrictions”.
Bessent said he wanted answers from Nvidia and its internal investigation of Jensen Huang’s behaviour within the next 10 days.
One analyst downplayed the prospect of a Huang return, describing the notion of the ex-CEO’s reinstatement as “ridiculous”.
Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives, said the range of issues facing Huang and Nvidia, from personal conduct to questions over China, made an external candidate or the permanent appointment of the interim CEO – Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress – the best option.
“We see no chance Jensen comes back to Nvidia as CEO and for the company the best path forward is with a new external CEO or Colette,” he said, describing the petition as “noise and distraction”.
US lawmakers have said Donald Trump’s administration must answer questions on what it knew about Huang’s relationship with the suspected Chinese spy.
after newsletter promotion
Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before the House select committee on China, as well as the foreign affairs and the intelligence committees. The dates of the appearances, likely to be behind closed doors, have not been confirmed.
On Sunday, Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company where Alice Haung was an executive until she left in 2025, said it was a “ legitimate and lawful business ”.
In the past three years, the company was one of Nvidia’s biggest foreign customers, buying nearly $5bn (£3.8bn) in AI chips and advanced hardware.
Alongside Musk, the tech heavyweight signatories on the letter calling for Jensen Huang’s return include Tim Sweeney, the founder and CEO of the video game publisher Epic Games, and Garry Tan, the president of Y Combinator, San Francisco’s most renowned business incubator.
Another signatory, the Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, wrote that Huang had “erred, yes – to err is to be human – but I do not believe anything he has done rises to the bar of separating him from his company”.
More than 7,500 signatories identified themselves as Nvidia employees, equivalent to 18% of the company’s workforce.
The support illustrates the unique standing of Huang, who is seen within the industry as a godfather of AI . Under his leadership, Nvidia became a pivotal Silicon Valley investor, financing datacentres and startups, earning it the nickname “the central bank of AI”.
But the company – which will report on its quarterly earnings on Tuesday – has also faced criticism that it has fuelled a speculative investment bubble. Huang fought any constraints on the AI race, clashing on these issues with the Claude creator, Anthropic, and its chief executive, Dario Amodei. Agence France-Presse and Reuters contributed to this report

Russell as they discuss the warnings surrounding artificial intelligence and how we can separate fact from speculation. Livestreamed only. Book tickets here or at guardian.live

articles.title_orig: New Zealand tricks and annual leave - the lengths fans are going to for GTA 6
articles.title_zh: New Zealand tricks and annual leave - the lengths fans are going to for GTA 6
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto fans have waited 13 long years for the latest edition of the game to be released - and going to extreme lengths to be ready for its launch.
GTA 6 will be released at midnight on Thursday - and Victoria Evans, from West Sussex, is not leaving anything to chance.
She has her alarm set for 05:00 GMT, and has a day off booked. She says she put the game's release on her leave request form which was approved, she told BBC News, despite the fact her boss "doesn't know what GTA 6 is".
She's far from the only one. For the game's launch day, HR software company BrightHR looked at absence data from more than 1.2 million employees from 70,000 businesses across the UK.
It found GTA was mentioned in 4.6% of time-off requests by employees. Throughout November and December, it said an estimated 83,000 days had been booked off for the game.
And booking leave is only one of the ways fans are making sure for the big day. Others are buying a new console to play it on or even pretending they're halfway around the world to get early access.
Market intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimates GTA 6 has already generated $1.18bn (£894m) from 12 million pre-orders - although Rockstar has not confirmed this.
Despite the option to preload the 212GB game, Jennifer Holmes, chief executive of the London Internet Exchange, said several UK internet providers including BT and Virgin Media had "increased capacity in anticipation of higher demand" ahead of launch.
Gamers have long been known to book time off work for major releases.
When Red Dead Redemption 2 launched in October 2018, social media users were sharing plans to take the day off, with one analytics firm reportedly finding more people talking about calling in sick for it than any other game that year.
Similar conversations took place ahead of Cyberpunk 2077's release in December 2020, with fans discussing taking several days off to play.
Some places have decided to lean into the trend for GTA 6 by offering incentives around the game - including the US Army's 3rd Infantry Division based at Fort Stewart, Georgia.
It gave some active-duty soldiers a four-day pass to play the game when it is released in November, as long as they sign a reenlistment contract for a minimum of two years between 1 August and 12 November.
"The idea was to have a unique incentives programme that connects to what soldiers are interested in," public affairs officer for the division, Lieutenant Colonel Angel Tomko confirmed to the BBC in August.
"There are 130 soldiers eligible within the battalion, and 20 have selected this incentive as part of their reenlistment," she said at the time.
Aside from taking time off, some gamers have also been discussing a technical loophole which could give them valuable extra hours of play before it officially unlocks in their country.
Because GTA 6 will release at midnight local time in all regions, New Zealand will become one of the first places where it is available, due to it reaching midnight earliest because of its position near the international date line.
This has led to some investigating ways to "trick" their consoles into thinking they're based in the island country when they are in fact thousands of miles away.
According to Google Trends, searches for the "GTA 6 New Zealand trick" have surged by more than 5,000% in the UK over the past month.
Games journalist Vic Hood said many gamers would be looking to play earlier to "get in on the action as soon as possible", as well as to prevent spoilers.
"As New Zealand is 13 hours ahead of the UK, that's 13 hours of gameplay that has time to spread across the internet and potentially spoil some key story beats and in-game surprises," she said.
"Took an extra day of paid time off when I found this out," one fan posted on Reddit on the trick.
It also means gamers would be playing the game at the much nicer time of 11:00 GMT, rather than having to stay up all night.
But another Xbox user shared caution on Reddit, noting that while the loophole had been exploited for many years for other game releases, GTA 6 "might be the game where Microsoft finally does something about this 'exploit'" - which could include  banning players.
GTA 6's developers Rockstar and publishers Take Two Interactive have not commented on the loophole, and neither have Sony nor Microsoft.
Louise Wooldridge from Ampere Analysis said both Microsoft and Sony had "rules governing regional accounts and purchases" for the Xbox and PlayStation, adding that Sony's were "slightly more restrictive".
Players who choose to use the workaround could therefore risk breaching those terms and conditions and potentially face restrictions on their accounts or lose access to their digital games.
Some gamers will have to wait even longer than their console-playing counterparts to get their hands on GTA 6, as the game will not be available on PC at launch, similar to previous GTA releases.
"Spare a thought for the PC users who will have to live vicariously through others' YouTube videos and Twitch streams," gamer Stephen Finn told the BBC.
A PS5 now costs from £520, while the more powerful PS5 Pro is nearly £790.
Despite the hefty price tag, for some the temptation to join the community in playing what many have called the biggest game launch of the year, if not decade, has been too great.
Reddit posts and videos, such as one by US YouTuber isoish , show fans buying consoles specifically to play the game.
"So, the only game I'm going to have on here is GTA," the content creator said in the video.
"The whole PS5 is for GTA 6."
After more than a decade of waiting, it seems some fans are determined not to waste a single minute of GTA 6's release - no matter the cost or extra effort.
Additional reporting: Kris Bramwell
